ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Hubert H. Humphrey — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: First visit to establish shared care three months after radical cystoprostatectomy with an ileal conduit for bladder cancer [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Wants his follow-up after bladder removal and his urostomy managed close to home and work. [S]
Bothered by appliance leaks and sore skin around the stoma, which interrupt his long working days. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Hubert Horatio Humphrey Jr. was born on 27 May 1911 in Wallace, South Dakota. [D]
Humphrey served in the U.S. Senate from Minnesota from 1949 to 1964, as vice president from 1965 to 1969, and again in the Senate from 1971 until his death. [D]

Humphrey sought medical advice in 1967 for blood in his urine; some doctors suspected bladder cancer, others disagreed, and he was not treated. In 1968 doctors found and removed several pinhead-size nonmalignant growths from his bladder. In 1994 researchers reported a p53 gene mutation in bladder cells from a 1967 urine sample of his. [D]
In 1973 doctors found possibly cancerous tissue in his bladder and treated it with thiotepa and X-ray therapy, given five minutes a day for five weeks. [D]

After three years free of cancer, an examination at the National Naval Medical Center in Bethesda for symptoms of a urinary tract infection found a low-grade malignancy, and in October 1976 a six-hour radical cystectomy at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center removed his bladder, prostate, lymph nodes, the fatty tissue around the bladder, and part of the urethra; the ureters were joined to a conduit made from a segment of small intestine, brought out to an opening on the skin to the right of the navel and drained into a bag. The nodes were to be examined for spread, and an experimental two-drug chemotherapy might be offered. [D]
He resumed his Senate duties in January 1977, serving as deputy president pro tempore from January 5, 1977. [D]

Urology consultation to share survivorship surveillance after radical cystectomy, review the stoma, and set the metabolic monitoring plan. Guideline: Holzbeierlein J, et al. Treatment of Non-Metastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/ASCO/SUO Guideline (2017; Amended 2020, 2024). J Urol 2024;212(1):3-10 (2024); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bladder Cancer (2026) [S]

Cancer surveillance after cystectomy for pT2a N0 disease: CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis every 6 to 12 months for 2 to 3 years, then yearly; no adjuvant therapy. Guideline: Holzbeierlein J, et al. Treatment of Non-Metastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/ASCO/SUO Guideline (2017; Amended 2020, 2024). J Urol 2024;212(1):3-10 (2024); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bladder Cancer (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, urologic cancer monograph (2026) [S]

Kidney and metabolic monitoring after an ileal conduit: chemistry with creatinine, chloride, and bicarbonate every 3 to 6 months in the first year, then yearly; upper-tract imaging every 6 months to year 3; vitamin B12 yearly; alkali for bicarbonate below 22 mmol/L. Guideline: Holzbeierlein J, et al. Treatment of Non-Metastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/ASCO/SUO Guideline (2017; Amended 2020, 2024). J Urol 2024;212(1):3-10 (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, urologic cancer monograph (2026) [S]

Stoma care with the wound, ostomy, and continence nurse: appliance fitting, peristomal skin care, and parastomal hernia checks. Guideline: Holzbeierlein J, et al. Treatment of Non-Metastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/ASCO/SUO Guideline (2017; Amended 2020, 2024). J Urol 2024;212(1):3-10 (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, urologic cancer monograph (2026) [S]

Urine infection plan with a conduit: no routine urine cultures or treatment of bacteriuria without symptoms; for fever, flank pain, or rigors, a culture taken by catheter from the stoma and prompt treatment; about 2 liters of fluid a day. Guideline: Holzbeierlein J, et al. Treatment of Non-Metastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: AUA/ASCO/SUO Guideline (2017; Amended 2020, 2024). J Urol 2024;212(1):3-10 (2024); Trautner BW, et al. IDSA 2025 Guideline Update on Complicated Urinary Tract Infections (2025) [S]

Distress screening at each visit, physical activity, and a written survivorship care plan. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bladder Cancer (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, urologic cancer monograph (2026) [S]
